territorial_scope.description: Applies to data centres and public bodies in Spain; takes effect on publication in the Spanish Official State Gazette (BOE).

evidence.quote: entrará en vigor el día siguiente al de su publicación en el «Boletín Oficial del Estado»

summary.short: Draft royal decree on data-centre energy efficiency. Operators with ≥500 kW IT power demand publish annual energy, water and employment indicators; owners above 1 MW must reuse waste heat; sites of 1 MW or more report best practices; grid access depends on compliance. Enters into force after BOE publication.
summary.long: Spanish draft royal decree implementing the waste-heat and reporting provisions of Directive (EU) 2023/1791 for data centres. Article 4 requires operators with IT power demand of 500 kW or more to report annually, by 15 May, the indicators under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364, plus minimisation strategies for specified indicators, employment estimates, and client and data location by country; the information is published on the ministry's website. Article 5 requires data centres above 1 MW nominal energy input to reuse waste heat, through a plan with a cost-benefit analysis (Annex I), regional assessment and municipal authorisation; a three-year voluntary period is followed by a mandatory two-year period. Article 6 requires data centres with IT demand of 1 MW or more to report how they apply EU Code of Conduct best practices; sites above 100 MW must show placement in the top 15% on specified indicators. Article 7 conditions grid access permits on compliance with Articles 4 to 6. Article 3(4) excludes facilities used exclusively for defence and civil protection. Enters into force the day after BOE publication.

notes: Draft RD (proyecto), no adoption date. The date of the public hearing, the Council of Ministers meeting and the signature are left blank ('…'). Article 1 cites only the Directive, not the Delegated Regulation. Article 3(2) addresses promoters and owners, but Article 5(1) addresses 'centros de datos'. Article 5(2) names the 'Ministerio para la Transición Energética', while Article 5(3) and other provisions name the 'Transición Ecológica'. The transitional provision cites 'artículo VI' of RD 1183/2020, where Article 7 cites its Chapter III. Article 4(2)(c) refers to Spanish skilled-employment rules without naming them. Relations to the Directive and Ley 24/2013 are stated only in the preamble.
